title: ICE Accountability in Minneapolis
subtitle: The surge may be ending, but accountability is just beginning

urgentBanner.text: The federal government is reportedly ending the "metro surge" in Minneapolis, but there has been no accountability for the lives lost, the communities harmed, or the constitutional violations committed. Now is the time to demand action while this is still in the national spotlight.

contentBlocks.label: Justice for Renee Macklin Good
contentBlocks.contextText: On January 7th, 2025, ICE agent Jonathan Ross shot and killed Renee Macklin Good in Minneapolis. No charges have been filed and no meaningful accountability process has begun.
contentBlocks.templateFragment: On January 7th, ICE agent Jonathan Ross shot and killed Renee Macklin Good in Minneapolis. To this day, no charges have been filed and no meaningful accountability process has begun.

contentBlocks.label: Justice for Alex Pretti
contentBlocks.contextText: On January 25th, a federal agent shot and killed Alex Pretti, a 37-year-old ICU nurse, in Minneapolis' Whittier neighborhood. This was the second fatal shooting by federal agents in Minnesota in less than three weeks.
contentBlocks.templateFragment: On January 25th, a federal agent shot and killed Alex Pretti, a 37-year-old ICU nurse. Two people killed by federal agents in three weeks, and still no accountability.

contentBlocks.label: Racial profiling and targeting people of color
contentBlocks.contextText: ICE enforcement operations in Minneapolis have disproportionately targeted communities of color. Residents report being stopped, questioned, and detained based on appearance alone — not specific warrants or probable cause.
contentBlocks.templateFragment: ICE enforcement in Minneapolis has disproportionately targeted communities of color, with residents stopped and questioned based on appearance alone rather than specific warrants or probable cause.

contentBlocks.label: ICE must follow court orders
contentBlocks.contextText: Federal courts have issued orders regarding ICE enforcement practices, yet there are documented instances of agents ignoring or circumventing judicial directives. No agency is above the law.
contentBlocks.templateFragment: Federal courts have issued orders regarding ICE enforcement practices, yet agents have ignored or circumvented judicial directives. No federal agency is above the law.

contentBlocks.label: Constitutional rights must be respected
contentBlocks.contextText: The Fourth Amendment protects against unreasonable searches and seizures. The First Amendment protects the right to peaceful protest. ICE operations in Minneapolis have violated both — through warrantless actions and by mischaracterizing peaceful protests as riots.
contentBlocks.templateFragment: The Fourth Amendment protects against unreasonable searches and seizures. The First Amendment protects peaceful protest. ICE operations in Minneapolis have violated both through warrantless actions and by mischaracterizing peaceful protests as riots.

contentBlocks.label: Reparations for community damage
contentBlocks.contextText: The metro surge caused lasting harm to Minneapolis communities — businesses disrupted, families traumatized, trust in institutions destroyed. The federal government must make communities whole for the damage caused by these operations.
contentBlocks.templateFragment: The metro surge caused lasting harm to Minneapolis communities — businesses disrupted, families traumatized, and trust destroyed. The federal government must make these communities whole.

contentBlocks.label: Children traumatized, especially in Columbia Heights
contentBlocks.contextText: Children across Minneapolis have been deeply impacted by the metro surge. Students in the Columbia Heights school district have been especially affected, with children afraid to go to school, families pulled apart, and kids left wondering if their parents will come home.
contentBlocks.templateFragment: Children across Minneapolis have been deeply impacted by ICE operations. Students in the Columbia Heights school district have been especially affected — children afraid to go to school, families pulled apart, and kids left wondering if their parents will come home. No enforcement policy is worth traumatizing children.

contentBlocks.label: Inhumane conditions at the Whipple federal building
contentBlocks.contextText: People detained at the Whipple federal building in Minneapolis have been held in inhumane conditions. Congressional visitors and advocates from The Advocates for Human Rights have documented dirty facilities, missing beds, inadequate blankets, minimal food, and extremely cold temperatures. Detainees lacked meaningful access to legal counsel — phones could not reach legal service providers, and handbooks with legal information were available only in English. DHS has denied all allegations, but firsthand accounts from elected officials and court-ordered inspections tell a different story.
contentBlocks.templateFragment: People detained at the Whipple federal building in Minneapolis have been held in inhumane conditions — dirty facilities, missing beds, inadequate blankets, minimal food, and freezing temperatures. Detainees have been denied meaningful access to legal counsel, with non-functioning phones and legal information available only in English. When members of Congress documented these conditions firsthand, DHS simply denied everything. Denials are not accountability.

tones.label: Democrat Rep
tones.subject: The Metro Surge Is Ending — Now Demand Full Accountability
asks: Criminal accountability for the agents who killed Renee Macklin Good and Alex Pretti
An end to racial profiling in federal enforcement — no one should be targeted for the color of their skin
Federal reparations for the Minneapolis communities damaged by the metro surge
Legislation requiring ICE to comply with court orders and respect constitutional rights
Independent oversight of detention conditions at the Whipple building and all federal holding facilities
A congressional investigation into the conduct of the metro surge
tones.closing:
Ending the operation is not enough. Justice requires accountability, repair, and systemic change so this never happens again.

Thank you for your leadership.

tones.label: Moderate
tones.subject: ICE Must Be Held Accountable for Minneapolis Operations
asks: An independent review of the metro surge operations and the two fatal shootings
Enforceable requirements that ICE comply with court orders and constitutional protections
Policy reforms to prevent racial profiling in federal enforcement operations
A fair process for addressing the damage done to Minneapolis communities
Independent inspection and enforceable standards for federal detention facilities
Oversight mechanisms with real enforcement authority
tones.closing:
The rule of law must apply equally to everyone — including federal agents. Accountability after the fact is the minimum we should expect.

Thank you for your commitment to oversight and the rule of law.

tones.label: Conservative
tones.description: Constitutional rights, limited government, law and order
tones.subject: Federal Agents Must Respect the Constitution and Court Orders
asks: Full accountability for the use of lethal force — including the deaths of Renee Macklin Good and Alex Pretti
Strict enforcement of court orders on federal agencies — no agency is above the judiciary
Constitutional protections against unreasonable search and seizure in enforcement operations
An end to blanket enforcement tactics that target people based on appearance rather than evidence
Enforceable detention standards — no American should be held in conditions that violate basic human dignity
Proper oversight of federal agencies operating in American cities
tones.closing:
A government powerful enough to ignore court orders and profile citizens without consequence is a government that has too much power. These are not partisan concerns — they are American ones.

Thank you for defending the Constitution.
